_comment: Curated lifecycle class for every FHIR R4 medication status code, answering one question: is this medication still being taken? The codes and their displays are NOT authored here: they come from the pinned FHIR R4 CodeSystem snapshots in sources/hl7-fhir-r4/, and the build fails if a FHIR code has no entry below or an entry names a code FHIR does not define. A code that appears in both MedicationRequest.status and MedicationStatement.status (active, on-hold, completed, entered-in-error, stopped, unknown) has ONE entry, so the two value sets cannot disagree about it.

classes.active: The source states the medication is being taken now.
classes.stopped: The source states the medication is not being taken: it ended, was withdrawn before use, or was never taken.
classes.unknown: The source states neither: the status is absent, unknown, paused, or describes an order or intention that has not started. Not evidence either way.
classes.entered-in-error: The record itself is repudiated. Not a statement about the medication at all; a consumer drops it rather than reading it as stopped.

active.why: FHIR: the medication is being taken, or the order is in force.

completed.why: FHIR: the course of therapy is finished.

stopped.why: FHIR: the medication was stopped before the intended course ended.

cancelled.why: FHIR MedicationRequest: withdrawn before any administration occurred, so not being taken.

not-taken.why: FHIR MedicationStatement: the medication was not consumed by the patient.

on-hold.why: FHIR: temporarily halted and expected to resume. Neither current nor ended; forcing it into either would be an adjudication the source did not make.

draft.why: FHIR MedicationRequest: an order not yet actionable, so nothing is being taken under it yet, but nothing has ended either.

intended.why: FHIR MedicationStatement: may be taken in the future. Not started, not ended.

unknown.why: FHIR: the authoring system does not know the status.

entered-in-error.why: FHIR: the record was entered in error and should not be read as a statement about the patient.

absent.why: MedicationRequest.status and MedicationStatement.status are both 1..1 (required) in FHIR R4, so a record that carries no status is one whose status is expected to exist but is not known, which is exactly FHIR data-absent-reason 'unknown'. Absence is not a statement that the medication is being taken.
